text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Many Finnish corporate directors to become millionaires as they convert options on their companies' stock.
- Former police chief to stand trial for receiving consultation fees while performing official duties.
- Army to admit women fighter pilots from next year.
- A majority of newly registered cars rust rapidly due to unfavourable weather conditions and salted roads. @
- Majority of Finns are opposed to Finland joining EMU, but are satisfied with EU membership, polls show. Finn's attitude towards single currency has remained steadily negative.
- Decision by European court to suspend EU poverty and old-age funding programme will not significantly affect Finland.
- Second earthquake measuring 2.8 on the Richter scale was registered in Ylitorni in the north of Finland.
- Many foreign students in the university of Helsinki would take extra courses if more were available in English. @
- KAUPPALEHTI
- In the next two years high unemployment will still sit side-by-side with a shortage of young skilled labour in industries, says Uusimaa region's labour executive, Hannu Paju.
- Investor and client confidence in Merita bank has set its shares on the rise.
- Competitiveness of Finland's metal industry compares favourably in international arena.
- Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto says Nordic dispute on alcohol regulation policy with the EU does not have to end up in court: the issue can be solved by agreement. @
- DEMARI
- Any EMU member whose deficit exceeds three percent of GDP may be fined up to 0.5 percent of the excess unless the deficit was caused by special circumstances, according to EU proposal.
- AAMULEHTI
- Finland to sign Schengen agreement removing border controls between EU members by Christmas.
- Voters in Euro election in Pirkamaa region not supportive of so-called "celebrity candidtaes", polls show.
- TURN SANOMAT
- Home of Finnish legendary Olympic athlete Paavo Nurminen to be refurbished for centenary. @
- Finland ready to sell old armaments to Estonia for training.
